label: RESPECT_2: the respect type of a constructed finite model
term: respect type of a constructed model
definition: A particular type constructed in Lean to serve as the respects of a finite model in a satisfiability, nonvacuity, omission or independence theorem: an inductive type with a few named elements (for example TruthCore.Causality.NecessarySimplePlurality.Respect with esse, drive and heat), or Bool or Unit standing in for respects in a control. Its elements are labels of the model's interpretation. What holds of them, for instance that there are exactly three respects or that two respects differ, is a fact about the model, not about the respects in which real beings are in act, moved, caused or more and less (RESPECT_1, with the content of DEF-RESPECT).
note: Recorded as the contrasting sense to the intended respect carrier, after the pattern of the schema-model sense of the case signature (definition d0c11dff, disambiguation fe91cc1f), so that a finite model's respect type is never read as a claim about respects in the intended interpretation (AGENTS.md, 'existence of a witness versus properties of the particular witness'). No binder is tagged with this sense: a model's respects are constructed constants, not parameters of a proposition. A declaration whose Respect binder is tagged RESPECT_1 reads that binder in its role as the corpus statement; applying the same declaration to a model type is a RESPECT_2 use. The linked Lean declaration is one example of such a type, not the definition of all of them.
